docs.title: Link rules (enforced at save AND at render; Apex re-validates) — updated by Phase 1 spike 2
docs.text:
• External: https: only. New tab → rel="noopener noreferrer".
  • Email / phone: mailto: and tel: are allowed but rendered as plain hrefs (never through GenerateUrl, which mangles them).
  • Portal: stored as a relative path (/alumni-directory, /news/abc?x=1), validated with ^/(?!/)[^\s]*$ (exactly one leading /, no scheme; //host is rejected as an open redirect). Resolved at render with NavigationMixin.GenerateUrl using standard__webPage, which adds the site base path (/alumni here) — so the JSON is portable between sandbox and prod. Never use comm__namedPage (case-sensitive, fails silently) or a raw href="/path" (would 404 at the domain root).
  • Picker suggestions come from the site menu (NavigationMenuItem, see Phase 1 spike 3); any relative path can also be typed.
  • Render real <a> elements (not <button>), call Navigate on click for single-page navigation, visible focus, decorative icons, unique labels.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• ustWidgetButtonEditor (child of ustWidgetRecordEditor): add / edit / reorder / delete, saves with the record's Save (EASY writes immediately and cannot edit). Uses stable ids, not array index. Section shown for widget types that support buttons (extend COMPONENT_SECTIONS).
  • ustWidgetButtons (shared renderer): used by ustStaticContent now and the hero widget later.
  • Apex: parse/validate/sanitize JSON, drop invalid entries, resolve tags in label/url, return a clean list on PortalWidgetDto.
  • Button size is its own picklist, Button_Size__c, separate from Content_CSS_Class__c, so a panel style and a button size can be combined (resolved during the build; see "as built").

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Apex: JSON sanitization, scheme allowlist, relative path rules, tag resolution in labels/URLs. Jest: editor add/edit/reorder/delete, renderer placement above/below, unsafe URL rejection.

docs.title: Phase 3 — as built (2026-10-15)
docs.text:
Verified in the dev org: editor (browser), real Experience Builder render of the Home page (links, base path, click behaviour), server cleaning for signed-in vs guest (anonymous Apex), Jest 228/228, Apex registry/tags/ buttons/controller all green, org-wide Apex failures unchanged at 80 (environmental), Code Analyzer: no High findings in shipped code.

Piece Where Fields Buttons_JSON__c (32k long text), Button_Placement__c (Below default / Above), Button_Size__c (ust-buttons-wide / ust-buttons-full), in the admin and guest permission sets objects/UST_Portal_Widget__c/fields/ Server cleaning + link allowlist + tag resolution + portal-link suggestions (98% coverage, 18 tests incl. javascript:, //host, backslash, tag-smuggling) classes/PortalButtons.cls, tests/default/classes/PortalButtons_TEST.cls Controller returns buttons, buttonPlacement, buttonSize; a widget with only buttons still renders; tag lookup also triggers on button tags classes/PortalWidgetController.cls Shared rules (options, validation, JSON format, preview resolution), mirrors Apex lwc/ustButtonRules/ Renderer: real <a> links, base path via GenerateUrl, safe new-tab, rows by alignment, size classes lwc/ustWidgetButtons/ Placement above/below the text lwc/ustStaticContent/, lwc/ustWidgetZone/ Editor: add / edit / reorder / delete, validation, site-page picker, open-draft guard lwc/ustWidgetButtonEditor/, wired into lwc/ustWidgetRecordEditor/ (preview uses preview-mode) ustDataTags gained MODE_URL + urlEncode (matches Apex EncodingUtil.urlEncode) lwc/ustDataTags/

How it behaves. Buttons are stored as versioned JSON and rewritten by Apex on every read: tags resolved (links: identifier tags only, URL-encoded), invalid buttons silently dropped, unknown style/alignment/icon fall back to defaults, label capped at 80 characters, portal links never open a new tab, only https: links do. The editor and the server enforce the same rules, but the server never trusts the editor.

Findings that shaped the build (do not rediscover). - lightning-record-edit-form only returns fields it is asked for (an input field on the form) or that are on the page layout. Buttons_JSON__c has no input, so after a reload the editor showed no buttons even though they were saved. Fix: an always-present hidden lightning-input-field for it in ustWidgetRecordEditor.html. Any future field edited by a custom component needs the same. - NavigationMixin.GenerateUrl must not run before the component is connected. The parent assigns buttons before attaching the child, so resolving in the setter silently failed and the portal link had no href in the real site (the editor preview could not show this because preview mode skips resolution). The renderer now resolves from connectedCallback and when buttons change afterwards. Two Jest tests fail against the old code. - Jest: mocking lightning/navigation with { virtual: true } makes the mock unreliable when the whole suite runs (passes alone, fails in the full run). Omit virtual: true for that module. - Jest: base-component stubs expose name / type as properties, not attributes (filter on the property). - Link regexes with control characters are built from strings (new RegExp) so no inline ESLint disable is needed; the generated pattern was checked against tab, DEL, U+0001, and backslash cases. - The page-picker list shows 8 entries in the dev org (Home + the 7 menu pages) with a "login required" note; suggestions are only returned to users who can edit widgets, so portal users never see site structure.

Known limits / follow-ups. - Buttons sit above or below the text only, not inside a paragraph. - Only external https/mailto/tel and portal paths exist as types (no event-registration or giving types yet). - The portal link menu comes from NavigationMenuItem for the network named Alumni (PortalButtons.SITE_NETWORK_NAME); change it there if the site is renamed. Pages not in the menu can be typed in by path. - Not tested: a published site with real guest traffic (caching of personalized buttons), and keyboard/screen reader behaviour beyond the semantics built in (real links, assistive "opens in a new tab" text, focus ring). - PortalWidgetController.getWidgetsForZone and a few helpers exceed Code Analyzer complexity thresholds (Moderate); not changed.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Hero image widget + S3 (built 2026-10-15; open questions answered with defaults, not yet reviewed by the owner; uploads not yet tested end to end)
Org state found at the start (dev scratch org)
docs.text:
• AWS_S3_Directory_Image Named Credential still has the placeholder URL (https://REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_BUCKET.s3.REPLACE_WITH_REGION.amazonaws.com). Apex reports the same value. Until it is set to the real bucket, uploads cannot work and the tool would store placeholder addresses. The External Credential (AwsSv4, named principal) exists; keys were not inspected.
  • CSP trusted sites: AWS_S3_Directory_Image = the prod bucket stthomas-salesforce-directory-images-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (img-src only) and UST_AWS_S3 = https://static.aws.stthomas.edu (img/connect/font/style).
  • The bucket name says prod: no test objects are uploaded from scratch orgs without an explicit go-ahead.

docs.title: How the S3 tool really behaves (read from the deployed source; do not rediscover)
docs.text:
• File key = md5(orgId + recordId) + fileNameSuffix + extension. A null suffix becomes the literal text null (verified in Apex), and the later lookup searches hash. and never finds it, so the editor always passes a suffix: -hero (desktop) and -hero-mobile (mobile).
  • It writes the image URL to the record field itself (its own Apex update, in user mode, needs Read/Edit FLS on that field) and then fires a RefreshEvent (lightning__refresh). It never reports the URL to the parent. So the hero URL fields are not inputs on the record form (a later Save would overwrite the fresh URL with the form's stale copy); the editor reads them with getRecord and refreshes with notifyRecordUpdateAvailable when the refresh event arrives.
  • Resizing happens in the browser (canvas) with image-max-width / image-max-height and image-mode crop or resize; output is always PNG. It needs an existing record (a new, unsaved widget has no Id).
  • Only users with the dependency's AWS_S3_Directory_Image permission set can upload. Our permission set cannot include it (it lives in the dependency), so widget admins need both. config_dev already assigns it to System Administrators.
  • The dependency component is not in this repo; it must be installed in an org before our templates that reference c-aws-s3-directory-image will deploy (CumulusCI does this through cumulusci.yml dependencies).

docs.title: Decisions (defaults chosen to keep moving; all are single-line changes)
docs.text: Topic Decision Content Reuses the Static Content fields: headline = Static_Content_Header__c, overlay text = Static_Content__c (tags, headings, links), buttons + placement + size from Phase 3. Width Fills its zone (the zone decides width). Image is object-fit: cover. Height Hero_Height__c: Short (12rem), Medium (20rem, default), Tall (30rem). min-height, so long text never clips. Smaller on phones. Text position Hero_Text_Position__c: Left (default), Center, Right; vertically centered. Overlay Hero_Overlay__c: Light, Medium (default for a new widget), Strong, or blank (--None--) for no overlay at all. Changed 2026-10-16: it was first built with no "none" so white text always had contrast; the owner expected --None-- to show the picture as it is, and blank was silently becoming Medium. Blank now means none in Apex, the banner, and the editor preview; an unknown value still falls back to Medium. Help text warns that white text can be hard to read on light pictures. Mobile image Optional second upload (-hero-mobile); shown with <picture> below 48em. No image yet Solid brand purple, so text is still legible and the widget works before S3 is configured. Alt text Required in the editor once an image exists; an image without alt text is rendered as decorative (alt=""). Image sizes Desktop crop 1600x600; mobile crop 800x640. Cache The server appends ?v=<widget SystemModstamp ms> so a replaced image is not served stale (S3 key never changes). Image URL safety Server accepts https: only, no whitespace/quotes/angle brackets/commas/backslash; the browser CSP (img-src) is the second wall. Class access UST_Portal_Widget_Admin was missing PortalButtons (called directly by the Phase 3 editor): added in this phase.

docs.title: Known limitation
docs.text: Links inside the rich text on a hero keep the browser's default link color because lightning-formatted-rich-text cannot be styled from outside; use a button for calls to action on a hero.

docs.title: Phase 4 — as built
docs.text:
Piece Where Fields Hero_Image_URL__c, Hero_Mobile_Image_URL__c (Url), Hero_Alt_Text__c, Hero_Height__c (short/medium/tall), Hero_Text_Position__c (left/center/right), Hero_Overlay__c (light/medium/strong); Component_Name__c value ust_hero_banner; admin (edit) and guest (read) permission sets objects/UST_Portal_Widget__c/fields/ Image-address allowlist, cache-busting ?v=, defaults, alt text; getHeroImages for the editor (100% coverage, 10 tests) classes/PortalHero.cls, tests/default/classes/PortalHero_TEST.cls Controller adds hero to the DTO for hero widgets only; headline, text, and buttons use the existing tag and button handling classes/PortalWidgetController.cls Banner renderer: picture + optional mobile <picture> source, dark layer, text position, brand-colour fallback, load-error fallback (16 tests) lwc/ustHeroBanner/ "Over a picture" styling (white text, readable outline buttons) added to the shared renderers lwc/ustStaticContent/, lwc/ustWidgetButtons/ (overImage) Zone registry entry and template branch lwc/ustWidgetZone/ (3 render tests) Editor: Hero section with the two S3 uploaders, alt text, height, position, overlay, hero preview, alt-text gate; Reset now also restores the header lwc/ustWidgetRecordEditor/ (15 new tests) Jest stand-in for the uploader dependency (outside force-app, never deployed) and its moduleNameMapper jest-stubs/awsS3DirectoryImage/, jest.config.js UST_Portal_Widget_Admin also grants PortalButtons (missed in Phase 3) and PortalHero permissionsets/

Verified in the dev org. Real Experience Builder render of the Home page with a sample picture (served from a temporary scratch-only CSP entry that was removed again): picture loaded, object-fit: cover, mobile <source> for max-width: 767px, alt text, white 40px headline with the tag resolved, both buttons legible (solid + outline), portal link /alumni/alumni-directory. Editor on the record page: both uploaders are the real dependency component with the right suffix and crop size, no image-URL field is on the form, labels read Headline and Overlay text, the panel style is hidden, and Save leaves the two image addresses untouched (changed the overlay, saved, queried). Jest 272/272; Apex hero/buttons/tags/registry/controller tests green; org-wide Apex failures unchanged at 80 (environmental); Code Analyzer: no High findings. The test widget was restored to its exact original values.

NOT verified: an actual upload. The dev org's AWS_S3_Directory_Image Named Credential still has the placeholder URL, and the uploader returns AWS S3 request failed: received status 503. The bucket is named "prod", so no test objects were uploaded. Remaining checks once the credential points at a bucket you are happy to test in: upload a desktop and a mobile picture, confirm both addresses appear in the preview and on the record, replace one and confirm the new picture shows (cache-busting), delete one, and confirm the ?v= address works against the real bucket policy.

Findings that shaped the build (do not rediscover). - LWC reserves property names starting with on (LWC1108), like data; the "shown over a picture" property is overImage. - The uploader needs a saved widget (it uses the record Id). A new, unsaved widget shows "Save the widget first". - The uploader's lightning__refresh event bubbles and would reload the record page (losing unsaved edits); the editor stops it at its own boundary and re-reads only the two addresses (PortalHero.getHeroImages, not cacheable). - Mock call history leaks between Jest tests unless cleared; the new tests clear getHeroImages in beforeEach. - The Salesforce CLI mangles JSON in --values for sf data update record; use anonymous Apex for such updates. - The hero reuses the Static Content fields for headline, text, and buttons, so the existing "Preview as a guest" switch, tags, and button rules all work on a hero without extra code.

Setup per org before pictures can be uploaded (cannot be automated: secrets and environment-specific): 1. Set the Named Credential AWS S3 Directory Image Url to the bucket (https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com). 2. Set the CSP trusted site AWS_S3_Directory_Image to the same bucket URL with img-src checked (and any other host that will serve the pictures, such as a CloudFront domain). 3. Enter the AWS Access Key and Secret on the External Credential principal (Named Principal). 4. Assign AWS_S3_Directory_Image (from the dependency) and UST_Portal_Widget_Admin to widget admins. config_dev already assigns both to System Administrators. 5. Republish the site after changing CSP or permission sets, and give each hero widget a Hero Image Field FLS (done in UST_Portal_Widget_Admin and the guest set).

Bug found and fixed after Phase 4: switching a widget to Hero Banner showed no Hero section. Reported as "the S3 upload and options are missing". Opening a widget that was already a Hero Banner worked, which is all the Phase 4 browser checks covered; changing the type on an existing widget did not. Cause: lightning-record-edit-form fires load again whenever its field list changes (here, when the hero fields join the form), and each repeat reports the saved values. handleLoad copied them over the editor, so the Component Name dropdown still showed the new choice while the editor state snapped back to Static Content (any other unsaved edit was exposed the same way). Fix: the editor initialises once per record (_initialisedRecordId) and ignores repeat loads; handleReset and handleSuccess now also restore/track the widget type. Five Jest tests added (three fail without the fix). Verified in the browser by switching the Static Content TEST widget to Hero Banner. Lesson for later phases: test the change path in a real browser, not only the load path; Jest's single synthetic load could not show this.

Editor layout (2026-10-16). Each part of the form is its own card, in a fixed order: Widget Setup, Content, Call-to-action buttons, Hero Banner (hero widgets only), Preview, Audience Filters. Content is always directly below Widget Setup and Preview is always directly above Audience Filters (pinned by tests for Static Content, Hero Banner, types with no content, and after switching type). Card titles are 20px bold with a UST-purple underline. The button editor no longer draws its own heading (the card title names it). To move the Hero Banner card, move its one <template lwc:if={showHeroSection}> block in ustWidgetRecordEditor.html.

Signed-in portal users: permission set, sharing set, and sample users (2026-10-16). Signed-in alumni on the LWR site had no access to any portal Apex or to the directory fields. The old Alumni Community User profile belonged to the earlier Aura site and is not used here, so access is granted by two things, both proven by a test that runs as a real Customer Community user (Alumni_Portal_User_TEST, 4 tests): - Alumni_Portal_User permission set (force-app): the 6 controllers a portal page calls, read on the directory, business directory, news and widget objects with only the fields those controllers read (no email, phone, birthdate, or street address; found by running the controllers as the user and adding what each missing field broke), the Alumni_Business record type, and edit on the person's own profile fields. The public business directory (AlumniBusinessDirectoryController) now runs in system mode because guests read it, so it needs no field grants: only 9 Professional_Directory__c fields remain, for the profile and connected-profile pages. The guest set Alumni_Portal_Guest_User also grants that controller and the Alumni_Business record type, because the record type lookup is per user even in system mode. In system mode the controller's SELECT list and WHERE clause are the only gates on what a guest sees, so review them when they change. Favorites stay in Alumni_Favorites_User. Assign both to portal users; this is the grant for production too, not just scratch orgs. - Sharing Set Alumni Directory Edit Own (unpackaged/config/portalSharing, task create_community_portal_sharing_set, config_dev step 5.8): maps Alumni_Directory__c.Contact__c to the user's own Contact with Edit. Without it a portal user can read but cannot edit their own profile (UserRecordAccess edit=false, every update fails with INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS_ON_CROSS_REFERENCE_ENTITY, even from a without sharing class). A permission set cannot fix that. It applies to the Customer Community Login User profile. For EDA-Staging or production, check whether an equivalent sharing set exists by hand and deploy this one if not. - Sample users (config_dev steps 90 to 92): the alumni dataset loads the people, create_sample_portal_users makes users smp1 to smp4 and assigns both permission sets, link_sample_portal_users sets Contact.Portal_User__c and Alumni_Directory__c.Community_Profile__c. Idempotent. The Alumni network stays UnderConstruction in a dev org until published, so the proof is the Apex test, not a browser login.

Existing gaps found on the way (not caused by this work). Contact.Community_Address_Range__c (a city and state formula used by the news search) and Contact.Degree_s_Formatted__c (business directory) were added to the repo on 2026-10-16. Alumni_Portal_User_TEST now calls the public directory and runs a news search as a signed-in user; the search failed for every portal user until Alumni_Portal_User granted Contact.Community_Address_Range__c. The Academic Majors widget filter does not work: the controller lines that load the user's majors are commented out (they referenced a Contact.Academic_Majors__c that does not exist), so any widget using that filter is shown to nobody. The data is on Alumni_Directory__c.Academic_Major_s__c (same Academic_Majors value set). Contact.Job_Title__c exists in the org but not in the repo source. Three older test suites (business directory, connected profile, my profile) fail in any scratch org because the Admin profile cannot use the Alumni_Business record type; the cause is the profile, not a missing field. The Alumni_Directory__c record type and field sets behind EDA-Staging may differ.

Record sharing (added after Phase 4). UST_Portal_Widget__c has an external default of Private, so signed-in portal users and the site guest could not read widget records directly (only through the without sharing controller). There are now two rules, both Read-only and both limited to Is_Active__c = true: - ShareActiveWidgetsWithPortalUsers shares with All Customer Portal Users (signed-in portal users). Lives in force-app/main/default/sharingRules/UST_Portal_Widget__c.sharingRules-meta.xml. - ShareActiveWidgetsWithAlumniGuest shares with the Alumni site guest user (community nickname Alumni). Lives in unpackaged/config/guestSharing/ and is deployed by the task create_community_guest_sharing (config_dev step 5.7), not with force-app. A guest rule fails to deploy ("Specify a guest user's nickname for the guestUser field", reproduced) until the site and its guest user exist, and force-app is deployed before create_community; keeping it in force-app would have broken every fresh cci flow run dev_org. The folder is raw metadata format (package.xml plus sharingRules/<Object>.sharingRules, no -meta.xml). For EDA-Staging or production, deploy that folder after the site exists.

Why: widgets are published content, and the pictures a Hero Banner points at must load for guests. Widgets hold no personal data: data tags ({{First_Name}} and so on) are stored as plain text and only resolved per viewer at render time, so a viewer who reads the record directly (for example through an Aura endpoint) sees the tag, not anyone's data. Do not type real personal details into widget text. Turning a widget off removes the share; turning it on adds it (checked in the dev org: 18 active widgets, 18 shares per rule, 0 for the inactive one, and a toggle added then removed both rows). Field access is still limited by the Alumni_Portal_Guest_User permission set.

Known limits / follow-ups. - Links typed inside the overlay text keep the browser link colour (use a button for calls to action). - The S3 tool always saves PNG (large files for photos), keeps the same file name when replacing (handled here with ?v=, but not for other uses of the tool), and has no responsive sizes or CDN. Candidate changes in the tool repo: JPEG ~0.85 for photos, a versioned file name, and a second size. - Inline images in Static Content are still not supported (see the decision above). - A hero is as wide as its zone; full-bleed width depends on where the zone sits in the page template. - The alt-text rule blocks Save when a picture exists; a "decorative image" option could be added if needed.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Visual refresh: match the look of alumni.stthomas.edu (5.0, 5.1 and 5.2 DONE 2026-10-19; 5.3 to 5.6 planned)
Decisions (confirmed by the owner 2026-10-19)
docs.text: Topic Decision Fidelity Match the live look closely (pill buttons, square shadowed cards, large Lora headings, full-width colour bands). Fonts Free fonts only. Lato and Lora are both OFL and are already bundled in staticresources/ustAlumniThemplate/fonts/ and loaded by ust-fonts.css via ustAlumniTheme.js. No Typekit, no new CSP entry. (The live site uses a UST Typekit kit; the faces are the same families.) Sources of truth 1) docs/Gemini-Brand-Refresh-Changes.md (Spring 2026 brand refresh, written for the Gemini CMS), 2) measurements of the live site (below), 3) current code. We re-create the look with our own CSS and our own images; we do not copy their stylesheet.

docs.title: What the live site does (measured 2026-10-19 at a 1280px window; screenshots were in ai-logs/screenshots/, not tracked)
docs.text:
Area Live value Body Lato 400, about 17.9px / 1.5 line height, black. Page background white. H1 (hero) Lora 400, about 56px, white. H2 Lora 400, about 47px, #510c76 (white on purple bands). H3 and below Lato (brand refresh), card titles 24px. Primary button Pill (border-radius 144px; guide says 9rem), fill #9e28b5, white text, padding about .75em 1.5em, 2px transparent border, 0.3s transition. Hover (guide): on light backgrounds fill #510c76 with white text; on dark backgrounds fill white with purple text; no outline. Band ("Panel") Full-width, padding 48px, margin 48px 0, min-height 576px, 64px gap. Backgrounds: white, gray #f6f6f6, light purple, purple #510c76, dark purple #340e51. Text card at left, picture at right overlapping the edge, with a large circle shape behind (filled and outline, purple or emerald). Hero Variant A: dark #230e3c with a faint shapes artwork, text left, photo right, breadcrumb under it. Variant B (home): full-bleed photo fading to purple, H1 over the picture, "eyebrow" links with arrows along the bottom (line colour is emerald). Not measured yet: mobile layouts, hover and focus states (the live CSS is cross-origin and unreadable, so those come from the guide), the exact fluid type formula (sizes scale with window width).

docs.title: Differences between today's code and the target (found in this review)
docs.text:
• Heading weight is 600 in ust-branding.css (--dxp-g-font-weight-heading); live H1/H2 are 400. Heading sizes are 36/26/20px; live are about 56/47/24px.
  • Static Content's heading uses slds-text-heading_medium (about 20px) in the default (Lato) face; it should be a Lora H2.
  • Buttons are SLDS rectangles; the callout and inverse panel styles have a 4px radius and a left rule that the live site does not use.
  • ustWidgetZone.css and ustPortalWidgetStub.css still hardcode the old #4f2d7f purple and gold #c9a227.
  • Widgets hardcode hex values instead of using the --ust-* tokens defined on the theme.
  • --dxp-c-button-* makes base Lightning buttons a dark-purple rectangle.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
5.0 Calibrate (small). Measure the live site at 1440, 1024, 768 and 375px to derive clamp() type sizes and breakpoints; screenshot our current pages as the "before"; confirm the open colour values above with the owner. Spike: confirm that --ust-* tokens set on the theme :host reach widgets slotted into the page (they should inherit through the slot; not yet checked), and that a shared CSS module (@import 'c/ustSharedStyles') deploys and renders in an LWR site. Done when: a measured token table is added to this section and both spikes have a recorded answer.

5.1 Foundation tokens and primitives. In ustAlumniTheme.css and ust-branding.css: add the colour tokens, fluid type tokens, heading weight 400 for H1/H2, Lato for H3 and below, card shadow, pill radius, button padding, transition, shared focus ring. Add lwc/ustSharedStyles (CSS-only module) with the pill button, animated text-link underline, arrow-link and heading rules, so each widget imports one source. Replace the stray hardcoded hex values. Change the --dxp-c-button-* hooks so base buttons look like the primary pill. Done when: Jest unchanged and green; a page of plain headings, paragraphs, links and a base lightning-button matches the live site in side-by-side screenshots.

5.2 Template tweaks (ustAlumniTheme). Decide and build: (a) how a widget goes full-bleed while its content stays within 1280px (the .ust-main area has no container today; check what the Experience Builder section wrapper adds before choosing a technique, since the 100vw trick is fragile with scrollbars); (b) page background white versus the 10% gray in BRAND-COLORS.md (live is white with gray bands: recommend white); (c) a breadcrumb under the hero/banner slot; (d) a header and footer fidelity pass against the live site (nav height, spacing, footer columns); (e) skip link and focus ring unchanged. Done when: a full-bleed band and a contained widget can sit in the same zone and line up with the header on a 1280px and a 375px screen.

5.3 Restyle the shipped widgets. - ustStaticContent: H2 as Lora at the new size, purple (white on dark bands); link colours per the guide. Keep the existing Content_CSS_Class__c values working so sample data and any saved widgets do not break: ust-content-inverse becomes the Purple band, ust-content-callout a Light Purple band without the left rule, centered and muted unchanged. - ustWidgetButtons: pill primary (light and dark hover per the guide), secondary as an animated-underline text link, eyebrow arrow link (bold, no caps, underlined by default), keep the Button_Size__c options. ustButtonRules/editor preview must show the same look. - ustHeroBanner: add the split variant (text left, photo right on dark purple with a faint shape), keep the full-bleed photo variant, add the emerald line. New picklist value on a new field Hero_Layout__c (Full picture, Split), default Full picture so existing heroes are unchanged. Done when: Jest green; the editor preview and the live widget match for each style; contrast pairs are only from BRAND-COLORS.md (white on emerald is large-text only: do not put small white text on emerald).

5.4 Section backgrounds and accents (Static Content and Hero). New picklists on UST_Portal_Widget__c (not overloading Content_CSS_Class__c, which is single-select; same reasoning as Button_Size__c): Section_Background__c (White, Gray, Light Purple, Purple, Dark Purple) which also sets heading, text, link and button colours automatically, and Section_Accent__c (None, Green circles, Purple circles) for the decorative circles. Circles are CSS or inline SVG (no image requests). Permission sets, editor field and preview updated; docs/WIDGET-CATALOG.md updated. Done when: all 5 backgrounds x 3 accents render, pass the contrast table, and the editor preview matches.

5.5 New widget types (each = the 3 registry changes in AGENTS.md). In order of value for the Support page: 1. Card Grid (the "How You Can Make an Impact" block): 2 to 4 columns, picture, linked title, text, bottom bar (emerald by default, none allowed; one setting for the whole grid, per the guide). 2. Links List: arrow rows (with and without a picture), with the hover motion from the guide. 3. Story / Testimonial: portrait with circle accent, quote, attribution. 4. Events cards: deferred until the event data source is chosen. Design question to settle first: where card/link/story items live. Recommendation: a child object UST_Portal_Widget_Item__c (lookup to the widget; picture URL, alt text, title, text, link). Buttons are JSON because they have no pictures; items need a picture each, and the S3 uploader keys files on a record Id, so each item needs its own record. Needs: object, fields, sharing rules (active parent only, as for widgets, including the guest rule outside force-app), permission sets, an items editor in ustWidgetRecordEditor. Done when: the Support page block from the live site can be rebuilt by an admin with no code.

5.6 Verify and document. Side-by-side screenshots against the live URLs at 1280, 768 and 375px (BackstopJS or Playwright; widgets are guest-visible, so a published guest page is testable, but the dev org's Alumni network stays UnderConstruction, so use Experience Builder preview or EDA-Staging); Jest for every new class and allowlist; keyboard and focus check on pills, links and arrows; reduced-motion respected for the hover movement; Lighthouse accessibility; update WIDGET-CATALOG.md, MAIN_GUIDE.md, BRAND-COLORS.md (new tokens), AGENTS.md.

docs.title: Phase 5.0 and 5.1 — as built (2026-10-19)
docs.text:
Colour decisions (owner, 2026-10-19): use the live site's values. Dark Purple = #340e51 (token --ust-purple-deep, same as --ust-nav-bg), Gray band = #f6f6f6 (--ust-band-gray).

Measured token table (live site, support page; window widths include the scrollbar; sizes are linear in vw, so each is one clamp()):

Token 375px 768px 1024px 1440px Expression used Body 16.1px 16.9px 17.5px 18px clamp(1rem, .96rem + .208vw, 1.125rem), line height 1.5 H1 (Lora 400) 48.2px 51.7px 54.0px 56px clamp(3rem, 2.8rem + .9vw, 3.5rem), line height 1.1 H2 (Lora 400) 32px 38.7px 43.0px 48px clamp(2rem, 1.6rem + 1.7vw, 3rem), line height 1.2 H3 (Lato 400) 20.7px 22.3px 23.3px 24px clamp(1.25rem, 1.2rem + .4vw, 1.5rem), line height 1.45

Other live measurements: page side padding 18px at 375, 31px at 768, 39px at 1024, 48px from about 1265 (about clamp(1rem, .33rem + 3.33vw, 3rem)); content has no 1280px cap (a 1920px window gives a 1344px grid with 281px side padding, bands full width); card grid 1 column at 375, 2 at 768, 3 from 1024; card gaps 2em (rows) and 1em (columns) of the body size; card picture 3:2; card text padding 0 24px; band (Panel) is a column below 768px (padding 24px 24px 128px) and a row from 1024px (padding 48px, gap 64px, min-height 576px from 1440px); card hover shadow 0 16px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.2) (the brand guide says change the bottom bar to bright purple 8px instead: follow the guide); text-link underline is a 1.5px gradient background that is present at rest and slides away on hover; pill hover on the live site was inconsistent, so the guide's rule is used.

Spike answers. - Tokens set on the theme :host do reach widgets slotted into the page (ustWidgetZone resolves --ust-purple-lt and --ust-font-size-h2). Widgets can use var(--ust-*) freely. - @import 'c/ustSharedStyles' works on the platform (deploys, renders; the H2 in ustStaticContent comes from it). Under Jest it needs a stand-in: the import compiles to a JS import and a CSS-only module has no JS file. jest.config.js maps it to jest-stubs/ustSharedStyles/ (outside force-app, never deployed). Any future CSS-only module needs the same mapping line.

What was built. - ust-branding.css: bright-purple pill hooks (--dxp-c-button-* and, found by measuring, the brand-variant hooks --slds-c-button-brand-*, because --dxp-c-button-* alone left .slds-button_brand at #510c76), button radius and padding hooks, bright-purple default links, fluid body size, and a new :root:root block at the end for the type scale (see findings). - ustAlumniTheme.css: new colour tokens (--ust-purple-deep, -lt, -lt-25, -md, -md-70/30/20/10/5, --ust-band-gray, --ust-black-10), --ust-shadow-card, --ust-radius-pill, --ust-button-padding, --ust-transition-ui, focus ring tokens, fluid H1/H2/H3 tokens, line height 1.5. - lwc/ustSharedStyles (CSS-only): .ust-h1/.ust-h2/.ust-h3, .ust-link (animated underline), .ust-button and .ust-button_outline (with .ust-on-dark variants), reduced-motion respected. - First consumers: ustStaticContent (H2 is now ust-h2: Lora 400, fluid) and ustWidgetButtons (pill shape and padding, bright-purple focus ring, text link is now ust-link; the slds-button_* classes stay, so the existing tests still pin them; migration to ust-button is in 5.3). - ustWidgetZone.css and ustPortalWidgetStub.css: the old #4f2d7f purple and gold are gone (tokens with brand fallbacks).

Findings that change later steps (do not rediscover). 1. The site's branding set overrides our hooks. Experience Builder's Theme panel data (sfdc_cms__brandingSet/Build_Your_Own_LWR) injects an inline :root rule with its own --dxp-s-text-heading-*, --dxp-s-body-* and --dxp-s-html-font-family values. A plain :root rule in ust-branding.css loses to it, so the type hooks are repeated in a :root:root block (higher specificity, wins). Hooks we do not repeat still come from the Theme panel. 2. Several hook names in the old file were never read by anything: --dxp-g-font-size-heading-large/medium/small and --dxp-g-font-weight-heading. The real names are --dxp-s-text-heading-<extra-large|large|medium|small|extra-small|extra-extra-small>-font-size|font-family|font-weight|line-height and fall back to --dxp-g-heading-font-family. Mapping: H1 = extra-large, H2 = large, H3 = medium. These were replaced. 3. The official Salesforce docs return 403 to automated fetches; hook names were confirmed by reading the compiled stylesheets in the dev org (browser, document.styleSheets). 4. Builder text blocks authored as Bold keep weight 700 through the block's own hook (--dxp-c-text-block-font-weight); that is content, not theme. 5. After a static-resource deploy, wait for it to finish before reloading Builder (the org stamps the upload a few seconds after the CLI returns; a parallel reload measured stale CSS and nearly sent this investigation the wrong way). 6. Opening Builder: Setup, Digital Experiences, All Sites, Builder link; direct URL is /sfsites/picasso/core/config/commeditor.jsp?siteId=<0DM id> on the my.salesforce.com domain (the dev org's Alumni site Id is 0DMjZ0000001K7y). The canvas is the live-preview iframe.

Verified (dev org, Experience Builder canvas at 1920px). Theme font Lato at 18px / 27px; Lora and Lato files load; Static Content H2 Lora 400 at 48px (40px on the dark band); Builder H2 text block Lora 48px, H3 Lato 24px; all three button styles are pills (radius 144px, padding 12px 24px, Lato); brand button fill rgb(158,40,181); --slds-c-button-brand-color-background-hover resolves to #510c76 with white text and no outline rule (real :hover cannot fire inside the Builder overlay, so hover is verified through the resolved hook values and the SLDS rule, not by moving the mouse). Jest 284/284.

NOT verified / open. - Narrow widths (375px, 768px) of our own pages, the real hover and keyboard focus ring, and a published guest view (the dev network is UnderConstruction). - Site-wide effect on the other pages (directory, news, forms, profile): the body size, heading hooks and button hooks changed for every base component. Re-check those pages at the start of the next session. - The arrow link (.ust-arrow-link) planned for the shared module is deferred to 5.3/5.5, where it is first used. - Deployed to the dev org only; not committed.

docs.title: Phase 5.1 follow-up — SLDS skills review (2026-10-19, same day)
docs.text:
Ran the SLDS tooling from the Salesforce skills against the 5.1 files and used platform-docs-get for the official hook list.

Tools and how they were used. - SLDS linter: npx @salesforce-ux/slds-linter@latest lint <one directory> (takes exactly one directory; run once per component). All findings are warnings, no errors. - design-systems-slds-validate analyzer: node <skill>/scripts/analyze-quality.cjs <component> --hooks-index <apply-skill>/assets/hooks-index.json. - design-systems-slds-apply hook lookup: node <skill>/scripts/search-hooks.cjs --prefix "--slds-g-..." (verified --slds-g-sizing-border-2, --slds-g-font-weight-4, --slds-g-font-line-height-base exist before using them). - platform-docs-get: the plain fetch is blocked (403), but browser-rendered extraction works. Official pages used: .../exp-cloud-lwr/guide/brand-hooks-text.html and, with the full hook tables, .../brand-hooks-map.html ("How --dxp Styling Hooks Map to Theme Panel Properties"). The page text is in document tables (tr rows), not innerText of main.

Results (linter warnings, before 5.1 / after 5.1 / after this review).

Component HEAD After 5.1 After review ustSharedStyles (new) – 19 2 (intentional) ustWidgetButtons 19 16 5 (0 no-slds-class-overrides) ustStaticContent 17 17 17 (unchanged, pre-existing) ustWidgetZone 21 16 16 ustPortalWidgetStub 20 14 14 ustAlumniTheme 7 7 7

Analyzer: every component scores 100 in Component Usage; one critical (A004, decorative lightning-icon without alternative-text) fixed with an empty alternative-text (the icon is aria-hidden, the label sits beside it, so the finding was a false positive in intent but the fix is free); remaining warnings are Q021/A021 in ustAlumniTheme.css (pre-existing: skip link) and one intentional T021. No invented --slds-g-* hooks (T051 clean). The manual review gate (loading/error/empty states, semantics) was not run: these are styling-only changes to existing widgets.

Decision: brand tokens are an accepted exception. The linter's no-hardcoded-values-slds2 suggests --slds-g-* colour hooks for UST colours. UST purples, emerald and the band colours are brand values with no SLDS equivalent, so they stay as --ust-* tokens with the raw value as the var() fallback (the pattern the apply skill itself recommends). Where an SLDS hook exists for a non-brand value it is used with a fallback (--slds-g-sizing-border-2, --slds-g-font-weight-4, --slds-g-font-line-height-base). The remaining ~60 warnings across the older files (spacing/rem values, the Builder-only dashed boxes, the skip link) were not part of this work and are left alone; fix them when those components are next edited.

Real bugs found and fixed (all pre-date or came from not checking hook names). 1. 16 hooks in ust-branding.css were read by nothing: every --dxp-c-button-*, --dxp-c-link-*, --dxp-c-badge-*. The documented and consumed names are --dxp-s-button-* (color, border-color, color-contrast, *-hover, *-focus, *-active, radius-border, padding-*, font-size, line-height), --dxp-s-secondary-button-* and --dxp-s-link-text-*. Fixed: old names removed, correct ones set in the :root:root block. The --slds-c-button-* workaround I added earlier in 5.1 was removed (it overrode the Theme panel). 2. Horizontal button padding needs per-variant hooks. The compiled .slds-button_brand (and _outline-brand, _neutral, _success, _destructive, _text-destructive, _inverse) rules set inline padding from --slds-c-button-<variant>-spacing-inline-start|end and end in a hardcoded 1rem, so --dxp-s-button-padding-inline-* never reaches them. Block padding does follow --dxp-s-button-padding-block-*. Now set per variant (1.5em); measured 13.5px 27px for an 18px button, matching the live site. 3. ustWidgetButtons.css overrode .slds-button, .slds-button_outline-brand (lint no-slds-class-overrides). Replaced with our own ust-widget-button layout class and, for the on-picture look, the --dxp-s-secondary-button-* hooks scoped to .ust-buttons-on-image. Text links keep to ust-link only. 4. Remaining dead hooks (4, pre-existing, harmless): --dxp-g-root-contrast-2, --dxp-g-font-weight-body, --dxp-g-font-weight-bold, --dxp-s-section-spacing-block-start (the -end one is read). Left in place; remove when ust-branding.css is next tidied. Re-run the audit (snippet below) after any edit to this file.

Hook audit snippet (run in the Builder canvas iframe console or Playwright frame.evaluate): fetch ust-branding.css, list every --dxp-*/--slds-* it defines, and report those never referenced as var(--name in the other stylesheets' rules or inline <style>s. Run on 2026-10-19: 87 defined, 4 unread (above).

Verified after the fixes (dev org, Builder canvas). Brand, outline-on-picture and neutral buttons: radius 144px, padding 13.5px 27px, Lato 18px, fill rgb(158,40,181) (brand), rgba(0,0,0,.25) with white border and text (outline on picture), white with bright-purple text (neutral); hover hooks #510c76 / white; Jest 284/284; platform links resolve to rgb(158,40,181) underlined. Not re-verified: a text-link (ust-link) button (none on the Home page), real mouse hover, narrow widths, the other pages.

docs.title: Phase 5.2 — template tweaks, as built (2026-10-19)
docs.text:
How pages are structured (found by tracing the DOM, do not rediscover). - The theme's <main> is full width with no padding. Page width and side padding come from Experience Builder sections (community_layout:section), whose inner .columns-content is capped by --dxp-s-section-columns-max-width (was 1240px) and padded by --dxp-s-section-content-spacing-inline-start|end (was 1rem). Below 1024px the section reads the …-inline-start-mobile / …-end-mobile hooks (also for the tablet range; measured at 768px). A section can override the cap with its own "Max Content Width" attribute (maxContentWidth, which writes --dxp-c-max-content-width); the theme header and footer sections set it to none. - Widget zones in banner and above_footer sit outside any section, so they are as wide as the page. Zones in body and sidebar sit inside a section's column. - A standalone copy of the Builder preview can be opened as a normal page for responsive checks: https://<org>.scratch.live-preview.salesforce-experience.com/alumni/?app=commeditor&view=editor&formFactor=LARGE&viewid=<id from the Builder iframe URL> (read the id with page.frames() in Playwright). Resize the window freely; no Builder iframe.

Decisions. | Topic | Decision | |---|---| | Content width | Match the live site: 1344px cap and the fluid gutter clamp(1rem, .33rem + 3.33vw, 3rem) (17.8px at 375, 30.9px at 768, 39.4px at 1024, 48px from about 1265). Set through Builder's own section hooks, no wrapper component. | | Full-bleed band | A band lives in a full-width region (banner, above_footer, or a section with Max Content Width none) and its content aligns to the grid with --ust-content-inset = max(gutter, (100% - 1344px)/2). A viewport-bleed hack (margin-inline: calc(50% - pageWidth/2)) was prototyped and works only in a centred single-column section; not built. | | Page background | White (live site). Gray #f6f6f6 is a band colour. | | Header | Content width 1440px with a 1rem edge (live), brand row 72px, nav row 64px, total 137px; tokens --ust-header-max, --ust-header-gutter, --ust-header-height. | | Footer | Content 1344px inside the page gutter; brand column Purple #510c76 running to the left page edge (clipped, no scrollbar); column split 1:2; contact links are brand-refresh pills (white fill on hover); column headings Lora with a thin white rule. | | Breadcrumb | Region only: a breadcrumb slot in ustAlumniTheme.html between the banner and <main>. It is empty (invisible) until something is placed there in Builder. No component built (see open questions). |

What was built. - ustAlumniTheme.css: tokens --ust-content-max (1344px), --ust-page-gutter, --ust-content-inset, --ust-header-max/-gutter/-height, --ust-container-max now follows --ust-content-max; page background white; footer brand colour --ust-footer-brand-bg = Purple. ustAlumniTheme.html: breadcrumb slot. - ust-branding.css (:root:root block): --dxp-s-section-columns-max-width: 1344px and the four --dxp-s-section-content-spacing-inline-* hooks (desktop and -mobile) set to the fluid gutter. - ustAlumniHeader.css, ustAlumniFooter.css: as in the table. Old 1280px / 1.25rem containers are gone. - ustHeroBanner: new @api fullWidth; with it the hero text lines up with the page grid (class ust-hero_full), without it the hero keeps plain padding because its section already supplies the gutter. ustWidgetZone sets it for the banner and above_footer zones (isFullWidthZone). Tests: 5 added (hero class follows the flag; the zone passes the flag for banner/above_footer and not for body/sidebar); both new behaviours were mutation-checked (fail without the fix).

Verified (dev org, standalone preview page; real window widths). - Section content: x=48, width 1329 at 1440; x=281, width 1344 at 1920 (the live site gives 48/1329 and 281/1344). Gutter 17.8 / 30.9 / 39.4px at 375 / 768 / 1024 (equal to the live values to a tenth of a pixel). No horizontal scroll at 1920, 1440, 1024, 768 or 375. - Header content starts at x=233 at 1920 (live: 233); header 137px tall at 1440; page background rgb(255,255,255); footer brand column rgb(81,12,118) with the bleed pseudo-element 1440px wide; contact buttons rgb(158,40,181), radius 144px, padding 12px 24px. - Banner-zone hero: band x=0, full width, text at x=281 / 48 / 31 / 18 (1920 / 1440 / 768 / 375) which equals the body grid's x at each width; body-zone hero: text at the same x. A throwaway banner-zone copy of the sample hero was used for this and deleted (0 left). - Seven other pages (directory, business directory, notes, my account, login, and the two error cases) keep the same 48 / 1329 content box, Lora H2 at 48px, pill buttons, white background, no horizontal scroll. - Jest 289/289. SLDS linter warnings (before 5.2 -> after): header 183 -> 181, footer 70 -> 68, theme 7 -> 7, hero 19 -> 16, zone 21 -> 16 (legacy counts in the header and footer are large and were not part of this work). Analyzer: no criticals.

Findings. 1. The footer's four link columns do not exist in this repo. The theme layout's footer region holds one Builder section with an empty rich-text block (<p><br></p>), and the header's navigation menu (Default_Navigation2, 10 items) is the only menu with items in the dev org. The live site's columns (Benefits & Resources, Get Involved, News & Events, Support St. Thomas) are content to create, not CSS. The footer's right two thirds is therefore empty today. 2. Full-page screenshots do not paint the sticky header's menu row (the nav looked empty in a full-page capture; a viewport capture and the DOM show all items). Use viewport captures for the header. 3. lawyer-search and news showed "Invalid Page"/view-load errors in the preview (a 500 loading the view script; news needs an article URL). Not caused by CSS, but a clean baseline was not run, so it is not proven pre-existing. 4. Percentages inside a custom property are resolved where the property is used (--ust-content-inset uses 100%), so use it for padding/margin on an element that spans the page.

Not done / open. - Header: the live header has a slightly different nav type size and spacing and an "audience" link group (Early Career Alumni, Parents & Families) and "Update Contact Info / Make a Gift" links; ours has none of these (content decisions, not CSS). Footer: the live legal links sit inside the left column and a "Back to Top" link is on the right; ours keeps a separate legal bar. The live footer has a faint shapes background image. - Not browser-verified: the real hover on footer pills, keyboard focus order across the new breadcrumb slot (empty), a published guest view. - Deployed to the dev org only; not committed.

docs.title: Phase 5.3 — restyle the shipped widgets, as built (2026-10-19)
docs.text:
Housekeeping first (owner decisions). No breadcrumb for now (the empty breadcrumb slot stays; the owner may want one later). The old Builder hero banner (dxp_content_layout:banner with a broken picture) was removed in the org by the owner; it is now removed from the bundle too: unpackaged/config/experiences/digitalExperiences/site/Alumni1/sfdc_cms__themeLayout/scopedHeaderAndFooter/content.json lost the banner and its five children (117 lines), and its component set now equals the org's (retrieved and compared by component id; the other byte differences were Builder adding empty dxpStyle objects, so the file was edited surgically, not replaced). A check-only deploy of the whole bundle passed (43 components). The older top-level unpackaged/config/experiences/Alumni1/ folder is not read by the sfdx-format deploy and still mentions the banner; it was left alone.

What was built. - Static Content panels (ustStaticContent): ust-content-callout is a Light Purple panel (square, 1.5rem padding, 2px emerald line under the heading); ust-content-inverse is a Purple panel (square, white text). Neither has a radius or left rule any more. The Purple panel tells its buttons they are on a dark background (new darkBackground property on ustWidgetButtons; not named onDark: LWC reserves public names starting with on). New darkBackground and largeHeading properties on ustStaticContent are used by the split hero. - Buttons (ustWidgetButtons, ustSharedStyles, ust-branding.css): the outline pill is now transparent with a bright-purple outline and fills Purple on hover (light backgrounds) or turns white with Purple text (dark backgrounds, and over a picture), done through the documented --dxp-s-secondary-button-* hooks. The solid pill's hover on a dark background also turns white (--dxp-s-button-*-hover hooks scoped to .ust-on-dark), because its normal Purple hover was invisible on a Purple panel. New style Arrow link (arrow_link) end to end: server allowlist (PortalButtons.cls), editor list (ustButtonRules.js), renderer (bold label, underline that slides away on hover, inline SVG arrow that nudges right, white on dark), shared CSS. The button row now centres its items (a text or arrow link next to a pill used to be stretched to the pill's height, leaving its underline 40px below the text). - Split hero (Hero_Layout__c, picklist full (default) / split): field + permission sets (admin edit, guest and portal read), PortalWidgetController query, PortalHero (DTO field, allowlist, default), ustHeroBanner (split template, CSS, fullWidth still applies), editor (picker, preview, hint, Reset). Split = #230e3c band, faint rings (CSS circles, clipped, aria-hidden), text left, 3:2 picture at most 560px wide bottom-aligned and hanging 2rem below the band; under 1024px the picture stacks under the text inside the band with 4rem below it. Text position and Overlay are not used in Split. New token --ust-purple-hero: #230e3c.

Verified in the dev org. - Split hero at 1440: text column x=48, picture 560x373 at x=817 (live site: identical); at 1024: text column 331px at x=39, picture 560px at x=410 (identical); at 768 and 375 the picture stacks inside the band with 64px below (live: 64px); no horizontal scroll at 1920, 1024, 768 or 375; headline Lora 56px white on rgb(35,14,60). - Real :hover states (forced through the DevTools protocol CSS.forcePseudoState; the Builder overlay blocks a real mouse): solid pill rest #9e28b5 and hover #510c76/white on light, white/Purple text on dark; outline pill transparent with #9e28b5 outline and #510c76 hover on light, white outline and white hover on dark; arrow link underline slides (background-position 0 -> 100%) and the arrow moves 4px. - Jest 307/307 (up from 289; 18 new tests, each mutation-checked: removing the behaviour makes a named test fail). Apex: PortalHero_TEST, PortalButtons_TEST, PortalWidgetController_TEST 43/43 in the org (new: layout chosen/default/blank/unknown, arrow_link allowlist, layout through the controller query). - The editor on the real record page: opening a split hero shows Split, switching the picker to Full picture and back repaints the preview immediately and shows/hides the hint. - Test data (3 ZZ_PROBE widgets in the banner and body zones; the picture was the repo's own alumni_picture_placeholder static resource, served from the site's own origin, so no trusted-URL or Named Credential setup is needed) was created for the checks and deleted; 0 left, the original sample hero is untouched.

Bug found in the editor by the real-browser check (pre-existing, fixed). The record form fires load several times and the first four do not contain the hero fields (they only join the form once the type is known: a recorded sequence was 4 loads without any Hero_* field, then 2 with them). handleLoad's "initialise once per record" guard (added in Phase 4 to stop later loads undoing edits) was used up by the first load, so an existing hero opened with defaults in the preview (Overlay none, Layout full) even though the saved values were medium/split. (Corrected in 5.4: Save writes these fields from the form inputs, which showed the right values, so nothing was written back wrongly; the preview and Reset were what was wrong.) Fixed: initialiseHeroSettings() reads the hero group the first time a load actually contains it (once per record), separately from the rest. Two regression tests reproduce the recorded load sequence; reverting either half makes one fail. Lesson: any editor field that only joins the form for one widget type must be read when it first appears, not on the first load. Jest could not have found this: its fake record always carries every field.

Other findings (do not rediscover). 1. Browser caches hide deploys. After a deploy the preview and the Lightning record page kept serving the old component for minutes. What worked: wait 20 to 30 seconds after the CLI returns, then clear storage with the DevTools protocol (Storage.clearDataForOrigin for indexeddb,local_storage,cache_storage,service_workers and Network.clearBrowserCache), load, wait about 25 seconds and reload once. Deleting IndexedDB from page script is not enough (open databases are deferred). Confirm by reading a changed hook or property from the page, not by assuming. Check the org first (LightningComponentResource source) so you know the deploy itself landed. 2. A forced :hover leaves the element looking hovered until the page is reloaded (a screenshot after such a check showed white pills at rest); reload before taking screenshots. 3. Field defaults apply to every new widget: non-hero widgets created in the probe got Hero_Layout__c = full. Harmless (it is ignored for them), and widgets that existed before the field have no value, which the portal treats as full. 4. Admin preview colours. The widget editor's preview (inside Lightning Experience) shows Salesforce-blue buttons, not the portal's purple: the --dxp-* brand hooks exist only on the site. For the solid button --slds-c-button-brand-color-background / -border and --slds-c-button-radius-border set on the preview container do repaint it (tested in the page), but the outline button's border has no hook that works in Lightning Experience (six names tried), so a partial fix would show a purple solid button next to a blue outline one. Not fixed; known limitation. The portal itself is correct. A fix would need either an explicit border/colour rule on the outline button inside the preview, or accepting the preview as layout-only. 5. The SLDS linter accepts layout literals with no hook (50rem rings, 100%, negative margins); these are commented as intentional in the split CSS. Hero warnings 16 -> 32 are those literals; spacing and borders use --slds-g-spacing-* / --slds-g-sizing-border-2 with fallbacks.

Not verified / open. - The arrow link and the split hero were checked at rest, hover (forced) and at four widths, but not with keyboard focus order or a screen reader; the arrow SVG and the rings are aria-hidden, the label carries the name. - A published guest view (the dev network is still UnderConstruction). - Sample data (datasets/widgets) has no split hero or arrow-link example; add one when convenient so a fresh scratch org shows the new looks. - Not committed.

docs.title: Phase 5.4 — section backgrounds and accents, as built (2026-10-19)
docs.text:
Scope. Static Content widgets only. The hero already has its own band and rings (5.3), so the pickers are hidden for it and overImage ignores them.

  • Fields (UST_Portal_Widget__c, restricted picklists, no default; blank means no panel / no circles): Section_Background__c (white, gray, light_purple, purple, dark_purple) and Section_Accent__c (green_circles, purple_circles). Admin edit, guest and portal read, in the three permission sets. PortalWidgetController queries them; PortalWidgetDto.sectionBackground / sectionAccent; ustWidgetZone passes section-background / section-accent.
  • Renderer (ustStaticContent): both values are allowlisted (BACKGROUND_CLASSES, ACCENT_CLASSES); unknown values are ignored. Purple and Dark Purple add ust-on-dark, which turns the heading, text, in-text links and buttons light (and the buttons get darkBackground, as in 5.3).
  • Older styles keep working. ust-content-callout is treated as Light Purple and ust-content-inverse as Purple (LEGACY_BACKGROUNDS). A chosen Section Background replaces them (their extra styling, such as the emerald rule under the callout heading, is dropped); centered and muted combine with any background. Existing records and sample data need no migration.
  • Circles are CSS only (a filled circle plus two outlines, top right, clipped by the panel, aria-hidden, 224px, 128px under 48em), so there are no image requests. Colors follow the brand guide's Feature Panel table: fill is Purple-tint for Gray, Light Purple, White; Dark Purple on Purple; Purple on Dark Purple. The line is emerald or Medium Purple 70%. White has no entry in the guide and uses the lightest tint. Circles need a panel (none without one).
  • Editor. Two pickers under the header (Static Content only), live in the preview, restored by Reset, and kept by Save.

Editor bug found and fixed (wider than 5.3 thought). A real-record check showed that the panel style, button placement and button size also arrive in a later load, not the first. The preview therefore got contentClass: "" for a saved Callout, and Reset never restored the class at all. Fixed once for all of them: LATE_FIELDS + initialiseLateFields() read each such input the first time a load contains it, once per record (the hero keeps its own helper). Save was never affected (it takes these values from the inputs). Rule: a new input that only appears for one widget type goes in LATE_FIELDS and gets a case in applyLateField, handleReset and handleSuccess.

Contrast, measured on 20 probe widgets (computed colors in the browser, WCAG ratios against the panel): headings 10.7 to 15.8; body text 12.6 to 17.4; buttons 5.2 to 15.8; links 5.2 to 6.1 on light panels and 12.6 / 15.8 on Purple / Dark Purple. The check caught a real failure: links inside the rich text were bright purple on Purple (2.1:1) and Dark Purple (2.6:1). lightning-formatted-rich-text reads --dxp-s-link-text-color, which passes through its shadow root, so .ust-on-dark in ustSharedStyles now sets that hook (and the hover one) to white. No horizontal overflow at 1440, 1024, 768 or 375. Circle outlines are decoration (about 2 to 5:1 against their fills), not information.

Double underline on the published site (arrow link and text link), fixed after 5.4. The widget editor preview showed one underline; the real site showed two. Cause, measured with a rule-by-rule listing of the stylesheets that match the anchor: the site's dxp-slds-extensions.min.css has a:link:not(.slds-button, ...) (and :hover, :active, :focus twins) that set text-decoration from --dxp-c-link-text-decoration / --dxp-s-link-text-decoration[-hover|-focus]. Its specificity beats our .ust-arrow-link { text-decoration: none }, so the anchor got a real underline on top of the label's drawn one. The editor preview runs in Lightning Experience, which does not load that stylesheet, so it never showed. Fix: .ust-link and .ust-arrow-link in ustSharedStyles set those three hooks to none, so the site rule itself resolves to none in every state (no !important). Verified on the site URL: computed none at rest, hover, focus and active, one underline in the pixels, on white and on Dark Purple. Rule: a plain text-decoration/color rule on an anchor in a component loses to the site's link rule. Set the --dxp-* link hooks on the element instead, and always check link styling on the site URL, not only in the editor preview.

Verification. Jest 328/328 (mutations caught: explicit background ignored, circles without a panel, dark list wrong, picture gets a panel, late fields read only on the first load, late fields re-read every load, Reset or Save forgetting the new fields, pickers shown for the hero). Apex 44/44 (PortalWidgetController_TEST has a new test for both fields and the blank case). Real Lightning record: pickers show saved values, the preview matches, a change updates it, Reset restores it. Sample data gains two widgets (a Light Purple panel with green circles, and a Dark Purple band with purple circles and an arrow-link button).

docs.title: Phase 5.5 — Card Grid, as built (2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Card Grid is done. Links List, Story / Testimonial and Events cards are not started (Events stays deferred until the event data source is chosen). Detail for admins is in WIDGET-CATALOG.md ("Card Grid"); the fields are in DATA-MODEL.md.

Design (measured from the live Support page first). Live: 3 columns at 1440 and 1024, 2 at 768, 1 at 375; gaps 1em and 2em; a white square card with 0 1em 2em black-10 shadow; a 3:2 cover image; 24px text padding; the title is a link stretched over the whole card; an 8px emerald bar along the bottom (a pseudo-element). The brand guide adds: one bottom-bar color for all cards (Green by default, with a None option), and the bar turns bright purple on hover instead of the shadow growing. - Data. New child object UST_Portal_Widget_Item__c, Master-Detail to the widget (so cards inherit its sharing, including the guest rule for active widgets, and are deleted with it; no new sharing config). Fields: Title (Name), Sort_Order__c, Card_Text__c (plain text, 500), Image_URL__c, Image_Alt_Text__c, Link_URL__c (text, so a site path like /alumni-directory is allowed), Open_In_New_Tab__c. Grid-wide settings on the widget: Grid_Columns__c (2/3/4, default 3) and Card_Bottom_Bar__c (green/none, default green); blank means the default, and unknown values fall back to it. - Apex. PortalCardGrid.prepare() is pure and reuses PortalHero.isAllowedImageUrl (https only) and PortalButtons.isAllowedUrl (the button link rules): a bad picture or link is dropped and the card is still shown; at most 24 cards. The portal query lives in PortalWidgetController (without sharing, system mode, one query for all Card Grid widgets on the page) because guests read it. The editor calls getEditorItems/saveItem/deleteItem/reorder/getGridPreview as the admin; saveItem applies the same rules but refuses with a message instead of dropping, and every edit or delete is scoped to the widget id so a card of another widget cannot be changed. UST_Portal_Widget_Admin was missing the class grant (caught by thinking about a non-System-Administrator editor, not by any browser run as sysadmin); PortalWidgetAdminAccess_TEST now pins the five editor classes. - Renderer. ustCardGrid composes ustStaticContent (new <slot> last, and hasSlotContent so the panel is drawn even with no text), so heading, text, buttons, Section Background and Accent are shared, not copied. Cards are white with their own dark text and purple links on any panel (the panel's light text and white links are inherited through the slot, so the card sets them again). - Editor. Cards section (Grid Columns, Card Bottom Bar, and ustWidgetItemEditor: add, edit, delete with a two-click confirm, move up/down, picture upload for a saved card). Cards save immediately (separate records, nested record forms are not allowed); the grid settings are late fields (LATE_FIELDS) and save with the widget. The preview asks Apex for the grid with the on-screen settings, so it applies exactly the portal's rules and nothing is duplicated in JavaScript; only the newest answer is used.

Bugs found by measuring, not by tests. 1. Hover bar never showed. In the compiled CSS LWC puts an attribute selector on every compound, so .ust-card-grid_bar[x] .ust-card[x]::after (4 specificity points) outranked .ust-card_linked:hover[x]::after (3). Both looked equal in the source. Fix: the bar color is a custom property (--ust-card-bar) that the hover rule changes, and the pseudo-element only reads it. Rule: when a state rule must beat a descendant rule in LWC CSS, change a custom property instead of racing specificity, and look at the compiled stylesheet when a hover does nothing. 2. Columns by window width were wrong. In the body zone the grid is narrower than the window (875px at a 1440px window), so 4 columns gave 189px cards. Columns now use a container query on the grid (rem, not em, in the thresholds, because em follows the container's own font size), with a window-width fallback in @supports not. 3. Card text size scaled with the window (14px at 375px); the live site is a fixed 16px. Now 1rem. 4. The title font looked like a bug (Lato, not Lora) but is the 5.1 decision: H3 is Lato on the live site too; only H1 and H2 are Lora.

Verification. Jest 394 (new: ustCardGrid 21, ustWidgetItemEditor 27, editor 15 more, Static Content slot 3), with mutation checks for every rule that guards data or work: link and picture re-validation, column and bar fallbacks, preview and modified clicks, uploader refresh, order, delete confirmation, the 24-card limit, scoping, late fields, stale preview answers (the overlap test first passed without its guard, because flushPromises here is a single microtask: read after the re-render). Apex 91 across the widget classes, PortalCardGrid 100%; mutations on scoping, link validation and reorder were caught. On the site URL with real data: order by Sort Order not title, a javascript: link and an http picture dropped, valid links work, no hover change on an unlinked card, keyboard focus ring drawn over the whole card, white cards on Dark Purple keep dark text and purple links, no horizontal overflow from 375 to 1920. In a real Lightning record (a script drove it as an admin): saved settings load, add, server refusal of a bad link and picture with a readable message and the form kept open, fix and save, preview follows, reorder, edit with pre-filled values, delete with confirmation, Columns preview without saving.

Not verified. The picture upload to S3 (no credential in the dev org, same as the hero): the uploader is present for a saved card with the right settings, and the editor re-reads the address after its refresh event (tested), but no file was actually uploaded. Pasting an https address is verified. Not run: a signed-in portal user and a guest viewing a Card Grid (the published guest page needs the site out of UnderConstruction); guest and portal read access to the new object and fields is verified by query, and the portal query is system mode.

Bug found after 5.5: "All Pages" widgets never showed (fixed 2026-10-20). PortalWidgetController still had AND Page_Context__c INCLUDES (:pageContext) in its SOQL, which only returns widgets whose stored value contains the requested page, so a widget stored as all was filtered out before widgetMatchesPage (which does accept all) ever saw it. The comment above the query already said the page check was meant to happen after the query. Every test chose the first picklist value, so none used all. The clause is removed; two tests now cover All Pages (several pages, several zones, a widget for another page not leaking). Confirmed with Apex on the dev org (banner and above-footer on home and alumni_directory__c went from 0 to 1) and by reading the org's theme layout, which places both zones with Layout scope. Not confirmed in a browser (no usable session at the time); open the home page to see the banner and the above-footer widgets.

Sample data. Two Card Grid widgets (6 cards on Gray; 2 cards, 2 columns, no bar, on Dark Purple), with no pictures so they work without S3. The recipe was generated offline with Snowfakery and its exact values inserted in a rolled-back savepoint to validate them (it also showed Snowfakery turns a quoted "3" into the number 3, which Bulk API serializes back to 3; picklist values stay strings in the file).

None exists as a widget yet; the guide's styles are recorded here so they can be built when a widget needs them.
